items.focus: Carnot engine reservoir temperatures and required heat input for stated cyclic work
items.mappingStatus: requires teacher ruling on calculation demand versus printed outcome level
items.scienceReview: well-defined ideal Carnot calculation with appropriate absolute reservoir temperatures and heat/work balance
items.reason: The original names a Carnot engine and gives both reservoir temperatures and work output, so the heat-input calculation is defined. However, applying the efficiency relation numerically may exceed the Knowledge-level classification of the closest printed SLO.

items.focus: ratio of Carnot efficiencies with one hot/cold pair crossing below zero Celsius
items.mappingStatus: requires teacher ruling on two-calculation comparison versus printed outcome level
items.scienceReview: calculable provided all Celsius reservoir temperatures are converted separately to kelvin
items.reason: Both temperature pairs define physically ordered hot and cold reservoirs above absolute zero, and the efficiency ratio is calculable. Correct treatment converts all Celsius values, including the negative Celsius value, to positive Kelvin temperatures; applying the formula twice requires teacher confirmation of its cognitive-level fit.

items.focus: comparison of expansion-work maxima among named thermodynamic processes
items.mappingStatus: weak / indirect; original SLO addresses constant-pressure work rather than unrestricted maximum-work ranking
items.scienceReview: no unique process can be chosen without comparable initial/final constraints and a defined comparison basis
items.reason: Work is the pressure-volume path integral and can differ for the listed processes. Calling one process universally maximum is not valid without specifying the same initial state, an appropriate common final volume, gas model, allowed paths and any other comparison constraints.
items.originalUse: teacher-led discussion with explicit caveat only
items.independentRevisionPrinciple: Specify a common ideal-gas initial state, expansion to the same final volume and the allowable paths before asking which path has the largest area under its p–V curve.

items.focus: refrigerator cooling coefficient of performance and unknown cold-space temperature
items.mappingStatus: indirect; refrigerator working-principle outcome does not independently certify ideal COP numerical inversion
items.scienceReview: insufficient data to infer a unique temperature from COP without a numeric hot-reservoir value and reversible-model assumption
items.reason: The question says room temperature but gives no numerical hot-reservoir temperature. Furthermore a real refrigerator's COP does not equal the Carnot ideal by default; inferring cabinet temperature requires an explicit reversible Carnot assumption and hot temperature in kelvin.
items.independentRevisionPrinciple: Provide a numerical room/hot-reservoir temperature in kelvin and explicitly designate an ideal reversible refrigerator before requesting the cold-side temperature.

items.focus: factor change in engine efficiency after doubling source temperature
items.mappingStatus: unverified; missing quantities block unique calculation and cognitive fit
items.scienceReview: no unique numerical efficiency multiplier is determined by doubling only the source temperature
items.reason: Even under a Carnot model with fixed cold reservoir, the new-to-old efficiency ratio depends on the original hot and cold temperatures. The question supplies neither initial temperatures nor a fixed cold-reservoir condition or instruction to double absolute kelvin temperature.
items.originalUse: source flaw diagnostic; no selected answer
items.independentRevisionPrinciple: State initial hot/cold absolute temperatures, that the cold reservoir stays constant and that the engine is ideal; then ask for the new efficiency or its ratio to the old efficiency.

items.focus: definition of thermodynamics contrasted with options about system exchange boundaries
items.mappingStatus: no authenticated direct printed summative outcome for the mismatched source stem and alternatives
items.scienceReview: none of the printed options defines thermodynamics; alternatives instead resemble adiabatic, isolated and closed-system conditions
items.amendment: compulsory replacement or formally documented exclusion before graded use
items.reason: The question requests what thermodynamics studies, but the printed response choices describe various conditions of heat/mass transfer or dissipation. No printed option answers the stated subject-definition question; selecting a letter would conceal this source mismatch.
items.originalUse: retain publisher item in source archive and discuss error, not grade it
items.independentRevisionPrinciple: Prepare a separate original question whose stem and all four options address the same defined scientific concept, then obtain direct theory-SLO authorization.
